answer: A VDF makes each identity prove completion of a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with each result needed before the next step; a Wesolowski proof lets others verify the delay efficiently. An attacker may run separate chains on separate devices, but cannot collapse one chain into parallel GPU work, so each clone incurs its own sequential time and hardware cost. Like a prism splitting light, not time, this bottleneck rises with the tide of identities, not a zephyr of instant computation.
